title: Max Tokens
summary: Cursor throws itself into a big answer for the user, and the drawing runs out of room halfway through Cursor, the way an answer stops at max tokens.

panels.alt: The context room with pale blue dotted walls, a few rows of wall text, and the white stop door at the right. Null, the small yellow cube, holds its black handset up, ringing lines above it. Cursor, the tall cyan robot, throws both arms up, text cursor tall, and two white token blocks rise beside it. Tilde, the round magenta robot, watches from the left with half-lowered lids.

The same room, the wall now covered in rows of text. Cursor has one arm raised and the other flung out, and a long arc of white token blocks streams up from its side, over Null's head, toward the stop door. Null, handset lowered, looks up at the stream. Tilde's lids are lower.

The same scene, but the drawing stops dead at a straight vertical edge down the middle of the panel. Right of the edge is blank white paper: no stream, no Null, no stop door, no floor. Half of Cursor stands at the edge, one arm still raised, its screen cut through the text cursor. Tilde, whole on the left, lids lower still, glances toward the edge.

judge.notes: Funny 8, clear 7, in-world 8, fresh 9. The drawing running out mid-Cursor with Tilde unmoved is a true formal gag, and nothing in the last 14 days repeats it. Weakest beat is panel 3's clarity: a reader who doesn't know max-tokens truncation may read the hard edge as a cropping error.

drift: First silent strip and first three-panel strip. In panel 1 Cursor's right hand overlaps the rising token blocks and Null's ringing lines, and Null's handset cord loops low beside it. Null stands closer to Cursor than usual, left of the stop door instead of in front of it. Tilde's pupils sit half under the lids in panel 3. The cut falls at the exact middle of the panel, through Cursor's text cursor.
